entries.title: White Sox' Davis Martin certain he isn't tipping pitches as he looks to bounce back
entries.summary: <p>Here’s a tip for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> right-hander Davis Martin’s start Thursday against the Reds: He’s 100% sure that he solved his tipping problem that the Red Sox exploited last week.</p><p>“It was actually a pretty easy one for me to fix, so I feel like we’re in a good spot,” Martin told the Sun-Times on Wednesday. “I like where my stuff’s at; I like where everything’s at from a tipping standpoint.”</p><p>That would be a relief for the Sox, who have watched Martin fall from an 8-1 record and 2.00 ERA through 11 starts to 9-6 with a 4.17 ERA through 23.</p><p>Martin technically will pitch on three days of rest, but his start Sunday against the Guardians, his first since the tipping, lasted just one inning because of a rain delay. And it was another bad first inning for Martin. He allowed two runs, giving him 12 first-inning runs in his last three starts.</p><p>Is that his next problem to solve?</p><p>“I’ve had plenty of great first innings,” he said. “I think over the course of the year, you’re just going to come through these blips where you’re going to have these struggles. I lean on things that I’ve learned.”</p><p>One of those things came from former Sox starter Lance Lynn in 2022, Martin’s rookie season. Lynn, then in his 11th season, told Martin that the biggest problem of his career was pitching in the first inning. So he began pitching the first inning in the bullpen, essentially, ramping up before taking the mound.</p><p>“I tried to do that a little bit this last outing, and I feel like the [velocity], the stuff and everything was there,” Martin said. “Obviously, the results weren’t there, but I liked how I was moving, how my pitches were moving. I liked the aggressiveness with which I was throwing. From a process standpoint, it was very good.”</p><p>But like he said, the results not so much. Though one run was unearned, Martin allowed two hits and a walk, continuing his struggles.</p><p>Pitching coach Zach Bove doesn’t put too much stock in the first-inning woes. He has a different explanation for Martin’s issue.</p><p>“Real simply, it’s the fastball execution,” Bove said. “Maybe that was a pitch that took some innings to get in a good spot, the locations and stuff. So dialing in from Pitch 1, if the fastball execution’s in a good spot, that makes the whole arsenal play up and obviously increases the odds that that first inning is going to go well.”</p><p>As for starting Martin on “short” rest, Bove said it was better than starting a rookie or calling someone up.</p><p>“We had the option to push him back. It’s not like we were forced to do this,” Bove said. “Talking with him, what’s the best matchup for our team and where we’re at, we just felt like this was the best option.”</p><p>But it will be an adjustment for Martin, whom the Sox told during the rain delay Sunday that pitching Thursday was a possibility. So he turned the day into his first day after a start, when he does lower-body weightlifting.</p><p>“Just trying to accelerate that process during the rain delay,” Martin said. “So great conversation between us, and that allowed me to get some of my routine done and almost treat it like a heavier bullpen.”</p><p>Bove said Martin threw a side session Tuesday that was shorter than normal and had a light throwing day Wednesday. On Thursday, Martin will try to recapture his old form.</p><p>“You can look at the mechanics, you can look at the pitch design, all that stuff,” he said. “But for me, it’s just mental stuff, like being more relaxed, stop pressing, stop trying to do too much and just be myself.</p><p>“That’s where my biggest thing is. We’ve gone down the rabbit hole of everything else. Now it’s just, mechanically, we feel good, we like where our pitches are. Now it’s just go out and have fun and execute those at a high level.”</p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Portage community cleans up after severe storm and deadly home explosion
entries.summary: <p>PORTAGE, Ind. — Joni Rainwater and her children were walking along Harrison Avenue Tuesday afternoon when the house in front of them suddenly exploded into flames.</p><p>The blast knocked them to the ground, and left her 14-year-old daughter covered in burning debris. Killed inside the home was Leona Rice, 86.</p><p>Neighbors helped Rainwater pulled the teen from the debris.</p><p>It all happened just as severe storms were beginning to sweep through the area, toppling trees, downing power lines and damaging houses and cars on Harrison and in surrounding neighborhoods. The storm also hindered emergency crews trying to respond to the explosion.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-cb0000" name="image-cb0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/4d18233/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6000x3367+0+316/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fd1%2Ffb%2F89ebd08f4d96b50ea0e31428ba72%2Fportagestorms-260813-2.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/aa0e0b4/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6000x3367+0+316/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fd1%2Ffb%2F89ebd08f4d96b50ea0e31428ba72%2Fportagestorms-260813-2.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a1d98f2/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6000x3367+0+316/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fd1%2Ffb%2F89ebd08f4d96b50ea0e31428ba72%2Fportagestorms-260813-2.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Trees felled by Tuesday's storms in Portage, Indiana were still in the road on Wednesday, August 12, 2026. entries.title: Brookfield Zoo prepares to welcome 2 dolphin calves
entries.summary: <p>On the heels of the sudden death of a newborn bottlenose dolphin last year, Brookfield Zoo is now expecting two dolphin calves later this year.</p><p>Two adult female dolphins, Allison and Allie, are both pregnant, zoo officials announced Wednesday. Allison is due late this summer or early fall, while Allie is due later in the winter. A due date hasn't been determined. Both dolphins are being closely monitored through blood tests and ultrasounds, and the fetuses look healthy and are developing normally, said Sathya Chinnadurai, Brookfield Zoo's senior vice president for animal health, welfare and science.</p><p>Last year, Allie gave birth to a male dolphin, the zoo's first birth in more than 10 years. But the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/museums-zoos/2025/06/12/baby-dolphin-brookfield-zoo-chicago-dies" >4-day-old calf died suddenly</a> after a meconium aspiration, meaning he inhaled fluid into his lungs, zoo officials said.</p><p>Now that both Allie and Allison are expected to give birth around the same time, the habitat will further simulate a wild environment, according to Rita Stacey, the zoo's senior vice president of programs and impact. Allison and Allie, like many pregnant and nursing dolphins, have been and will continue to spend more time together as they go through the gestation period together.</p><p>"We know that mothers that are pregnant at the same time tend to hang out together, and they actually form nursery groups when the little babies are born," Stacey said. "So we're really replicating nature here, and so we we are very excited to hopefully have a nursery in the very near future."</p><p>The meconium aspiration of Allie's calf last year couldn't have been predicted and doesn't mean Allie can't deliver a healthy calf, Chinnadurai said. The mothers and calves will be monitored closely, including 24-hour observation for the first month after birth, but the zoo is still prepping for unexpected obstacles.</p><p>"Even when everything goes according to schedule, we still keep a close eye just to make sure there aren't any unforeseen consequences," he said.</p><p>As soon as they're born, the calves' care teams will begin looking for them to hit certain development milestones, the first of which will be swimming to the surface of the water for a breath of air. They likely will begin nursing around eight to 10 hours after birth and closely watch their mothers to model their other behavior.</p><p>The calves will be introduced when it's determined they've both had enough time to bond with their mothers, and they're expected to interact and socialize with each other as well as their mothers, fathers and other dolphins. It's unclear which of Brookfield's two male dolphins fathered the calves, but the zoo plans to conduct paternity tests after each is born.</p><p>Each calf's sex also hasn't been determined. The calves will live with their mothers at Brookfield for the first years of their lives, but males will be separated from their family and transferred to a partner of Brookfield to avoid inbreeding. As male dolphins age, they spend more time further away from their mother and other dolphins, and between the ages of 5 and 7, they'll be ready to move.</p><p>Both Allison and Allie will need to get used to "feeding on the fly," or nursing their calf while swimming. Allie has given birth and raised calves before, but for Allison, a first-time mom, this will be a new skill.</p><p>The dolphin building will be closed for up to a few weeks after each calf is born to allow the mother and infant to bond, and zoo staff will determine when it's time to debut the calves to the public based on their development, Stacey said.</p>

entries.title: White Sox pope hat giveaway has some fans cashing in
entries.summary: <p>Thousands of White Sox fans attending Tuesday night's game got to take home a free hat fashioned in honor of team fan Pope Leo XIV. Now, listings for the exclusive pope hat are appearing online for sale. </p><p>Sellers on eBay and Facebook Marketplace are hawking the black-and-gold mitre hat featuring the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> logo. </p><p>One eBay seller is offering the hat for $129.99, and as of Wednesday evening, they've sold 15 hats with four still available. Other listings, advertising the pope hat as a "unique" and "collectible" item, noted their stock as unworn. Most hats found by the Sun-Times were selling between $50 and $100, but it's unclear if all of the hats are authentic.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" entries.title: 21 things to do in Chicago Aug. 13-19
entries.summary:
Theater

  • Kokandy Productions presents Stephen Sondheim and James Lapine’s masterpiece, “Sunday in the Park with George.” The musical considers poignant truths about life, love and the creation of art in a moving study of enigmatic painter Georges Seurat. Derek Van Barham directs. From Aug. 13-Nov. 11 at Chopin Theatre, 1543 W. Division St. Tickets: $55.20, $65.87. Visit kokandyproductions.com.
  • Matthew Libby’s drama, “Sisters,” explores the familial bond between Matilda and her AI sister Greta as their relationship begins to be tested like never before. Brenda Barrie and Chloe Johnston star; Jessica Thebus directs. From Aug. 13-Nov. 8 at Writers Theatre, 325 Tudor Ct., Glencoe. Tickets: $75+. Visit writerstheatre.org.
  • “Buddy – The Buddy Holly Story” is a tribute to the life and music of the rock and roll pioneer from his start in Texas to his meteoric rise and untimely death at the age of 22. Joey Chelius stars as Holly; Matthew D. Carney directs. From Aug. 19-Oct. 18 at Drury Lane Theatre, 100 Drury Lane, Oakbrook Terrace. Tickets: $85-$150. Visit drurylanetheatre.com.

  • Music Theater Works stages Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim’s classic musical, “West Side Story.” Set in 1950s New York, it’s the story of two warring gangs — the Jets and the Sharks — and the young lovers caught in the middle. From Aug. 13-30 at North Shore Center for the Performing Arts, 9501 Skokie Blvd., Skokie. Tickets: $19.50-$106. Visit musictheaterworks.com.
  • The Sweetest Season: A Gathering of Indigenous Creativity is a celebration of Chicago’s native and indigenous artistic community. Features a diverse array of events for all ages including a workshop for children and families, panels, a plant-pressing workshop, a poetry reading, an art exhibition and a performance of Arigon Starr’s “The New Adventures of Super Indian,” about a reservation boy with super powers who fights evil forces. From 11 a.m.-7:30 p.m. Aug. 15 at Goodman Theatre, 170 N. Dearborn St. Admission is free except for “Super Indian” ($10). For a full list of events, visit goodmantheatre.org.
  • Ryan Cunningham and Joshua Salzman took inspiration from Jane Austen’s “Pride and Prejudice” in creating the musical comedy, “I Love You Because,” a modern-day version of looking for Mr. Right. Scott Shallenbarger directs. From Aug. 14-Sept. 13 at Oil Lamp Theater, 1723 Glenview Rd., Glenview. Tickets: $55. Visit oillamptheater.org.
  • Over the course of one night in Tim Venable’s “Adolescent Salvation,” three teens banter, bicker and push each other to the edge of danger. Guillermo Cienfuegos directs. From Aug. 14-Oct. 3 at Theater Wit, 1229 W. Belmont Ave. Tickets: $18-$46. Visit theaterwit.org.
  • Nova Entertainment presents RJ Silva’s “Hail Mary/Maria,” a Filipino coming-of-age story about a shy kid who seeks help navigating his first crush. Adam Reed directs. From Aug. 14-22 at Theater Wit, 1229 W. Belmont Ave. Tickets: $25-$60. Visit theaterwit.org.

  • “This Is My Moment” is Dionna Griffin-Irons’ solo show blending essays, satirical songs and poetic prose to tell the real life story of a woman who has experienced the best life has to offer. Anthony Irons directs. At 7:30 p.m. Aug. 13-15 at Steppenwolf’s 1700 Theater, 1700 N. Halsted St. Tickets: $38. Visit steppenwolf.org/lookout.

Music

  • Since the release of his 2023 album, “Appaloosa Bones,” singer-songwriter Gregory Alan Isakov has been recording a series of song collaborations with fellow artists including Sylvan Esso, Noah Kahan, Nathaniel Rateliff, Shovels & Rope and Jeremiah Fraites (of The Lumineers). For his Ravinia performance, he’ll be joined by the Chicago Philharmonic for an evening of music and storytelling. At 7:30 p.m. Aug. 19 at 201 Ravinia Park Rd., Highland Park. Tickets: $59-$134. Visit ravinia.org.
  • The Salt Shed and the Empty Bottle present the return of the World’s Largest Karaoke Party, an event that gives audience members the chance to live out their rock star dreams. Singers are chosen at random through an on-site sign-up process. From 4-10 p.m. Aug. 15 at The Salt Shed, 1357 N. Elston Ave. Admission is free. RSVP at saltshedchicago.com.
  • Hometown Celebration is a benefit for the Lin Brehmer Scholars Fund featuring performances by The Linburgers (Matt Spiegel and Curt Morrison of Tributosaurus), Ike Reilly, Dag Juhlin, Michael McDermott, Heather Lynne Horton and more. At 7 p.m. Aug. 16 at Metro, 3730 N. Clark St. Tickets: $26, $31. Visit metrochicago.com.

  • Hailed as “Midwestern rock heroes” by American Songwriter, indie rock band Red Wanting Blue has spent the better part of the last three decades on the road. The songs on the quintet’s 13th studio album, “Light It Up,” are equally gritty and uplifting and an ode to hope and perseverance. At 8 p.m. Aug. 19 at Robert’s Westside, 7321 Madison St., Forest Park. Tickets: $25, $35. Visit robertswestside.com.

  • Black Ensemble Theater presents Fridays on the Green, a free outdoor music series featuring the soul-jazz sounds of The McNary Experience featuring Qiana McNary (Aug. 14), jazz saxophonist Mark Allen Felton (Aug. 21) and the Black Ensemble All-Stars featuring performers from the theater’s many productions (Aug. 28). From 6:30-8 p.m. at Clark Street and Sunnyside Avenue. Visit blackensembletheater.org.

Museums

  • “Conceived in Liberty: Cartoons, Caricatures and Illustrations in the Wartime United States, 1812-1918” shows how visual artists cheered, critiqued and satirized the country’s commitment to liberty during times of war. Included are political cartoons, magazine illustrations, caricatures, sheet music covers, broadsides and posters from the Newberry Library’s collection. To Sept. 19 at 60 W. Walton St. Admission is free. Visit newberry.org.

Family fun

  • The Chicago Air and Water Show returns with the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds, U.S. Army Parachute Team Golden Knights and other military performers from the U.S. Air Force, U.S. Marine Corps and U.S. Coast Guard. Civilian stunt performers include Kevin Coleman, Susan Dacy, Ed Hamill, Trojan Phlyers Flight Demonstration Team and more. From 10:30 a.m-3 p.m. Aug. 15-16 along the lakefront from Fullerton Avenue to Oak Street with North Avenue Beach serving as the show center. Admission is free. Visit chicagoairandwatershow.us.
  • Fan Expo Chicago, the comic and pop culture convention, returns with an all-star lineup including Kurt Russell; Mr. T; Elijah Wood, Sean Astin and Dominic Monaghan from “Lord of the Rings;” Corey Feldman, Martha Plimpton and Joe Pantoliano from “The Goonies;” William Shatner, Brent Spiner and Walter Koenig from “Star Trek;” “Halloween” director John Carpenter; and stars from “Smallville,” “Supernatural,” “The Boys” and more. From Aug. 14-16 at Donald E. Stephens Convention Center, 5555 N. River Rd., Rosemont. Tickets: $51+. Visit fanexpohq.com.

  • There’s something for everyone at the Illinois State Fair. Highlights include a carnival and circus, agriculture events and competitions, harness racing, auto racing, rodeo events, monster trucks, a wide array of food vendors and more. Among the Grandstand performers are Lainey Wilson, Ziggy Marley, Wiz Khalifa, The Avett Brothers, Drive-By Truckers, The Chicks, Shinedown and more. From Aug. 13-23 at Illinois State Fairgrounds, 801 E. Sangamon Ave., Springfield. Admission: $5, $10, children 12 and under free. Tickets for Grandstand shows vary. Visit statefair.illinois.gov.

Festival fun

  • Glenwood Avenue Arts Fest showcases artists from all disciplines plus children’s art activities, demonstrations, music and more. The festival kicks off with live music performances at the Cobblestone Jam from 6-10 p.m. Aug. 14 and then continues from 11 a.m.-9 p.m. Aug. 15 and 11 a.m.-7 p.m. Aug 16 at Morse Street and Glenwood Avenue. Admission is free. Visit glenwoodave.org.
  • Printer’s Row Art Fest brings together juried artists from across the country showcasing paintings, street art, jewelry, photography, sculpture, woodworking and more. From 10 a.m.-5 p.m. Aug. 15-16 on Dearborn Street from Harrison Street to Polk Street. Admission is free. Visit amdurproductions.com.
  • Little Italy Festa includes Italian food, music, cultural performances and exhibits, carnival rides and games, children’s activities and more. Music performers include The Bronx Wanderers, Hugo Valenti, La Tosca, Jersey Girls and many more. From 5-10 p.m. Aug. 13-14 and noon-10 p.m. Aug. 15-16 on Taylor Street from Ashland Avenue to Racine Avenue. Admission: $10 suggested donation. Visit oshows.com.

entries.title: Jacob Webb thriving in closer’s role as one of Cubs’ bullpen saviors: ‘The guy’s been a dog all year’
entries.summary: <p>WASHINGTON — Ask around, and you’ll find out that Jacob Webb has been a lot of things.</p><p>“He’s been nails, for sure.”</p><p>“He’s been awesome.”</p><p>“The guy’s been a dog all year.”</p><p>The right-hander has also been a savior in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ bullpen, stepping into the closer’s role unexpectedly with righty Daniel Palencia limited by injuries to just a handful of appearances this season.</p><p>Webb hasn’t racked up a huge number of saves, though his eight lead the team. But he’s delivered again and again, called on in games’ biggest moments to record the most important outs, whether they’ve come in the ninth inning or not.</p><p>He’s the closer, yes. But in Craig Counsell’s world of out-getters, he’s more accurately described as the Cubs’ go-to reliever.</p><p>And he’s thrived.</p><p>“You can see his demeanor on the mound,” lefty Ryan Rolison said. “He’s very laid back until his name’s called, and then it’s go time. You can see it in his eyes where he’s out there giving everything he’s got every single night.”</p><p>Webb, who came to the Cubs as a free-agent after three very solid seasons with the Angels, Orioles and Rangers, posting a 3.22 ERA. In 53 appearances this season, his ERA is 2.38. He entered Wednesday on a streak of 20 consecutive scoreless outings.</p><p>With the team still trying to emerge from an avalanche of midseason pitching injuries — Palencia, for example, is <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/05/cubs-daniel-palencia-jacob-webb-closer-craig-counsell-injury-rehab-kevin-gausman-trade-blue-jays-nl-central-standings-brewers" >still working back</a>, struggling in recent minor league rehab appearances — Webb has been an anchor, a steadying force.</p><p>Or, as one teammate put it:</p><p>“The guy’s been a dog all year,” fellow righty Trent Thornton said. “He takes the ball whenever his name’s called. He’s prepared. Everyone has the utmost confidence in him when he’s on the mound.</p><p>“He’s been given a great opportunity to step in and be the closer, and he’s taken the ball and ran with it. He’s got one of the most devastating changeups to watch. It’s, honestly, a sexy pitch.</p><p>“Just a dog. He’s a dog. That’s the best way to describe him.”</p><p>Webb, of course, isn’t the only bullpen arm the Cubs have asked <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/08/cubs-bullpen-ninth-inning-stats-jacob-webb-ryan-rolison-daniel-palencia-trent-thornton-tyler-ferguson" >to shoulder an unexpectedly larger role</a> amid so many injuries this summer, and he hasn’t been the only one to succeed.</p><p>It’s been a rewarding thing for his teammates who have stepped up in similarly big ways to see Webb take over the highest profile job in the relief corps and do it so well.</p><p>“It’s unbelievable,” Rolison said. “With some injuries and roles not being established early, guys going down and us having to step up into some bigger roles, to see him in that closing role? Anytime anything goes wrong we’re going to him. It’s been unbelievable to watch, just the consistency of it.</p><p>“Doing what he’s doing is really special right now.”</p><p>Playoff baseball brings all sorts of unexpected twists to the pitching puzzle, so we’ll see how Counsell opts to deploy his go-to reliever when the lights get their brightest in October.</p><p>But consider Webb battle-tested, according to his manager, seeing every type of hitter, including some of the best in the sport, and walking away the victor.</p><p>In back-to-back outings against the Dodgers last week, he worked through the heart of the order against <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-dodgers-tarik-skubal-tigers-jed-hoyer-trades-brewers-nl-playoffs-kevin-gausman-matt-shaw-injury" >baseball’s juggernaut</a>, retiring the likes of Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Kyle Tucker and Mookie Betts to lock down Cubs wins during a three-game sweep.</p><p>A week later, in the first game of a series against the Nationals on Tuesday, Webb got All-Star shortstop CJ Abrams to end the game as the potential tying run, polishing off a four-out save.</p><p>“The string of success he’s had, you have to do it against all the hitters,” Counsell said. “Sometimes, you get in the bullpen, you get in a run where you’re just facing the right guys, maybe.</p><p>“But you look at a night like last night, you’ve got to finish the game against Abrams. You’ve got to really earn it. You’ve got to get four outs, you’re really earning that stuff. That’s what I think Webby has shown.</p><p>“The matchup doesn’t matter, the situation doesn’t matter, he’s done it in every circumstance. And that’s what impresses you as much as anything.”</p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Last-place Stars fire head coach Martin Sjogren
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/stars" >Stars</a> have dismissed coach Martin Sjögren after less than a season with the National Women's Soccer League club.</p><p>Assistant coach Anders Jacobson was also let go by the Stars, the team said Wednesday.</p><p>The Stars (4-13-1) are in last place in the NWSL with a league-worst nine total goals scored, while allowing opponents 33 goals. The Stars have a five-match winless streak going into Friday's match at the Seattle Reign.</p><p>Sjögren, the former coach of Norway's women's national team, joined the Stars at the start of this season after a stint as coach for Hammarby in the Swedish Damallsvenskan.</p><p>Assistant coach Karina Báez will serve as interim head coach for the rest of the season. Former Stars head coach Lorne Donaldson will also rejoin the team as interim director of coaching for the season.</p><p>Donaldson, who led the Jamaican national team to the knockout round of the 2023 Women's World Cup, was let go by the Stars in April 2025 during his second season with the club. The Stars went 10-14-2 in his first season and made the playoffs.</p><p>"This is a group of players I truly care about, and I'm very happy to return to the Chicago Stars for the next several months," Donaldson said in a statement. "I'm excited to reunite with some familiar faces, for the opportunity to meet new players, and I look forward to working together with the staff to earn some wins in the final stretch of the season."<br></p>

entries.title: Browns to start QB Deshaun Watson vs. Bears on Saturday
entries.summary: <p>The Browns will start veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson against the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> on Saturday at Soldier Field.</p><p>Second-year player Shedeur Sanders figures to play the second half. Coach Todd Monken told reporters Wednesday that he wanted both Watson and Sanders to experience a two-minute drill at the end of their respective half against the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/12/bears-coach-ben-johnson-softens-his-tone-as-qb-caleb-williams-no-longer-drowning-in-offense" target="_blank" >Bears.</a></p><p>Sanders will start the Browns’ second preseason game. The two have generally split time with the first time during the first two weeks of training camp.</p><p>Watson will experience game action Saturday for the first time in almost two years. He suffered his first of two Achilles tendon tears on Oct. 20, 2024. He’s played just 19 games in Cleveland because of injuries and suspension. He was banned 11 games and fined $5 million in 2022 after being accused of sexual misconduct.</p><p>Sanders, who sank to the fifth round in the 2025 draft, threw seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in seven starts as a rookie.</p><p>Thursday, Bears coach Ben Johnson will announce which starters he plans to play Saturday.</p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module entries.title: Shedd Aquarium to receive four more beluga whales from Marineland
entries.summary: <p>Shedd Aquarium’s beluga whale population is about to double from what it was a month ago.</p><p>Four more of the white cetaceans are expected to leave the shuttered Marineland Canada this week, arriving in Chicago early Thursday if all goes to plan.</p><p>That’s a big “if,” given the storms that continue to sweep through the region.</p><p>On Wednesday morning, Shedd staff were in Niagara Falls, Canada, preparing the steel boxes used to transport the belugas — first by truck, then inside a Boeing 777 cargo plane flying from Toronto to Chicago, with one stop along the way: The same flight will also carry two more Marineland belugas headed to Georgia Aquarium.</p><p>“We are making sure we have everything that we need … from duct tape to making sure we have the appropriate foam and all the appropriate [beluga] stretcher sizes. This operation is so complex and every animal is different, and we tailor all of the transport equipment per animal,” said Charlie Jacobsma, Shedd’s director of animal behavior and training.</p><p>The incoming whales — all females, named Caspian, Peekachu, Rain and Secord — will join four other beluga rescues that arrived from Marineland July 21. In total, Shedd is expected to house 16 belugas, including the eight already living at the aquarium before the Marineland whales arrived.</p><p>The Marineland belugas, a group of 30, had been living at the park, which has for years faced criticism that its animals were living in unsanitary conditions. The park closed to the public in 2024 and Marineland officials, citing extreme financial difficulties, had threatened to euthanize the whales if permanent homes couldn’t be found.</p><p>None of the Marineland belugas has yet been put on display to the public at Shedd, and there is no timeline for when that might happen.</p><p>“If you have a rescue dog that is still learning to be confident in their new surroundings, you’re not going to take the dog to a dog park the first day that you have him and introduce him to all these new stimuli,” Jacobsma said.</p><p>The plan is to run some tests on the four incoming whales, and if the animals are found to be healthy, then they’ll be grouped with the four other rescued belugas.</p><p>Shedd uses a series of gates to separate the mammal groups.</p><p>“In some rare instances, some of the belugas at Shedd have shared the same space [with the Marineland whales], but mostly it has been through the gates,” said Shedd spokesman Johnny Ford.</p><p>The current goal is for Shedd to take a total of 10 belugas from Marineland, although an exact timeline for when the remaining two might travel to Chicago has not been determined, Shedd staff said.</p><p>Asked about the cost of the operation to remove all 30 whales — others are traveling to aquariums in Georgia, Texas, California and Spain — Ford said it is “projected to go into the millions,” primarily covered by the receiving aquariums.</p><p>Ford said the cost would not be passed along to Shedd visitors in the form of increased ticket prices.</p><p>“This is not what we had in our budgets this year, but it was something that we felt called to do as an obligation to these animals. This is something out of our own savings,” Ford said.</p><p>Andrew Burns, a longtime adviser and lawyer for Marineland, said Wednesday that the closed aquatic park has also committed “millions” to the move.</p><p>“All its available funds were committed to this move,” Burns said. “So we’ve made a massive financial commitment ourselves.”</p><p>With the expected departure of six belugas this week, Marineland will be left with 11 whales.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/museums-zoos/2026/07/22/belugas-chicago-shedd-aquarium-marineland-canada-rescue" >Rescued belugas have arrived in Chicago. The move is unprecedented — and controversial</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/museums-zoos/2026/07/23/canadian-belugas-rescue-shedd-aquarium-imminent-risk-lawyer-marineland" >Canadian belugas faced ‘imminent risk’ of death before emergency flight to Chicago, marine park lawyer says</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-history/2026/08/07/beluga-whale-shedd-aquarium-abbott-oceanarium" >When Shedd Aquarium’s first beluga whales came to Chicago</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Greater Grand Crossing woman’s death caused by heat stroke, medical examiner’s office rules
entries.summary:
A 94-year-old woman who died in July is the 11th person in Cook County whose death has been tied to extreme heat, according to the Cook County medical examiner’s office.

Claramont Little, of Chicago’s Greater Grand Crossing community, died in the early morning hours of July 2 in the same block where she lived, according to the medical examiner’s office. The medical examiner recently determined her death was caused by a heat stroke and it was ruled an accident.

Cook County has experienced the highest number of heat-related deaths in a single year in more than a decade, according to a WBEZ and Chicago Sun-Times analysis of data from the medical examiner’s office.

The others whose deaths have, at least in part, been attributed to the heat this year are Otto G. Kendzior, 64; Joseph Huff, 65; Robert Feldon, 77; Stephanie Rodriguez, 45; David Gonzalez, 44; Barbara Whigham, 71; Mike Rodriguez, 57; Daniel Machnikowski, 69; Victor Ferguson, 48; and David P. Sopys, 46.

entries.title: Macabro hallazgo en Chicago desata dudas sobre la supervisión de funerarias en Illinois
entries.summary: <p>Un macabro hallazgo en una funeraria del extremo lado sur está volviendo a revelar brechas en la supervisión gubernamental de instalaciones como la de South Deering, donde las autoridades hallaron docenas de cuerpos en descomposición <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/08/10/hallan-57-cuerpos-en-descomposicion-en-funeraria-del-extremo-sur-de-chicago" target="_blank" >la semana pasada</a>, según legisladores que el lunes pidieron una reforma a nivel estatal.</p><p>Pero antes de que Springfield vuelva a abordar el tema, las autoridades aún trataban de determinar quién podría haber evitado la pesadilla descubierta el jueves, aparte de la pareja de Evergreen Park acusada de manejar incorrectamente los restos de más de 100 personas en South Chicago Chapel, ubicada en el 2939 E. 95th St.</p><p>"Tenemos que encontrar la manera de adelantarnos a los malos actores", dijo el representante estatal Marcus Evans, el demócrata del lado sur cuyo distrito incluye la funeraria. "No queremos poner excusas. Lo que se hizo no fue suficiente".</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-840000" name="module-840000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Es la segunda vez en apenas dos años que los legisladores se ven obligados a responder a las espeluznantes acusaciones contra <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago/2026/08/07/owners-of-far-south-side-funeral-home-have-history-of-mishandling-human-remains" target="_blank" >Clark y Johanna Morgan</a>, los operadores de South Chicago Chapel.</p><p>Los Morgan también administraron un crematorio en Chicago Heights que el estado cerró el año pasado por el manejo indebido de los restos de unas <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2025/06/19/chicago-heights-crematory-bodies-death-license-closed" target="_blank" >100 personas</a>. Eso motivó una nueva ley estatal que amplió la autoridad reguladora de la oficina de la contralora de Illinois, que, por una peculiaridad de las responsabilidades estatales, supervisa crematorios además de sus funciones fiscales.</p><p>Pero la oficina de la contralora Susana Mendoza no regula a los directores de funeraria ni a los embalsamadores, quienes están licenciados por el Departamento de Regulación Financiera y Profesional de Illinois (IDFPR) en la administración del gobernador JB Pritzker. Y, al parecer, ninguna agencia estatal supervisa las funerarias en sí, en sus ubicaciones físicas, dijeron funcionarios.</p><p>"Necesitamos ver la posibilidad de ponerlo todo bajo un mismo techo", dijo la representante estatal Diane Blair-Sherlock, demócrata por Villa Park, quien copatrocinó la ley sobre crematorios de 2025 y afirmó que las instalaciones deberían estar sujetas a inspecciones trimestrales. "Pero ninguna de las dos agencias cuenta con el personal ni los recursos suficientes para hacer cumplir la ley… Así que creo que ahí es donde debemos mirar y preguntarnos: ¿dónde encajaría mejor esto y quién estaría dispuesto a asumirlo?".</p><p>Los funcionarios del IDFPR estuvieron "en el lugar" en Chicago Heights el año pasado, según la oficina de la contralora, que había "instado al IDFPR a retirar la licencia funeraria de Johanna Morgan" debido a las condiciones preocupantes del crematorio.</p><p>En noviembre de 2023, cuando a los 91 años murió el padre de Laura Godina, ella acudió a Heights Crematory en Chicago Heights para cremarlo. Unos meses después murió también su madre, de 89 años. Volvió a recurrir a Heights Crematory para la cremación. Pero algo siempre le inquietó porque su padre era mucho más corpulento que su madre.</p><p>"Me preocupa que la cantidad de restos de mi papá en la urna sea muy pequeña. Hay muy poco allí. Pero la urna de mi mamá está llena", dijo Godina. "Me preocupa lo que me entregaron".</p><p>"Me siento decepcionada porque los contratamos para un servicio. Pagamos por un servicio. Me siento triste y culpable porque confié en ellos —realmente confié— y me fallaron", agregó Godina. "No sé cómo trataron a mis padres, que eran lo más sagrado y lo más hermoso para mí. (Los Morgan) jugaron con mis sentimientos; me fallaron. Me siento tan decepcionada, tan decepcionada de ellos".</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-ee321a" name="image-ee321a"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8a8170c/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6576x3691+0+348/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F9b%2F5f%2F4c7d85ee4c418ca432f5c0235d01%2Ffuneralhome-260811-07.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/65b55cb/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6576x3691+0+348/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F9b%2F5f%2F4c7d85ee4c418ca432f5c0235d01%2Ffuneralhome-260811-07.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f4796d4/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6576x3691+0+348/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F9b%2F5f%2F4c7d85ee4c418ca432f5c0235d01%2Ffuneralhome-260811-07.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Laura Godina habla con una reportera de WBEZ el lunes sobre sus experiencias con Clark y Johanna Morgan en Heights Crematory, en Chicago Heights. Está preocupada por cómo el establecimiento manejó los restos de sus padres." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f4796d4/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6576x3691+0+348/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F9b%2F5f%2F4c7d85ee4c418ca432f5c0235d01%2Ffuneralhome-260811-07.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/bdfd8b4/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6576x3691+0+348/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F9b%2F5f%2F4c7d85ee4c418ca432f5c0235d01%2Ffuneralhome-260811-07.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f4796d4/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6576x3691+0+348/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F9b%2F5f%2F4c7d85ee4c418ca432f5c0235d01%2Ffuneralhome-260811-07.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Laura Godina habla con una reportera de WBEZ el lunes sobre sus experiencias con Clark y Johanna Morgan en Heights Crematory, en Chicago Heights. Está preocupada por cómo el establecimiento manejó los restos de sus padres.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Ashlee Rezin/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Clark Morgan ya había perdido su licencia de director funerario el año anterior por "conducta poco profesional" y en 2024 estaba operando con una licencia vencida, muestran los registros del IDFPR.</p><p>"También remitimos nuestros hallazgos y nos reunimos con la oficina de la Fiscal del Condado de Cook y con la [Policía Estatal de Illinois] con la esperanza de que se presentaran cargos penales", dijo la portavoz de la contralora, Kim Howard.</p><p>Una portavoz de la oficina de la Fiscal del Condado de Cook, Eileen O’Neill Burke, dijo que todavía no se ha materializado ningún caso penal potencial.</p><p>"Nos reunimos con [la Policía Estatal de Illinois (ISP)] y con la oficina de la contralora, que había referido el caso a la ISP, y recomendó que la ISP continuara su investigación y considerara la posibilidad de delitos financieros", dijo la oficina de la fiscal. "Posteriormente la ISP no se ha puesto en contacto con nosotros para revisar una investigación completada con miras a la consideración de cargos".</p><p>Un portavoz de la ISP dijo que su investigación del caso de Chicago Heights sigue en curso, mientras que los investigadores estatales están ayudando a identificar restos en el caso de South Deering "lo más rápidamente posible en medio de una situación horrible y extremadamente angustiosa".</p><h3>Respuesta estatal</h3><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a en un comunicado el viernes que su agencia "actuó con rapidez y decisión" para suspender la licencia de Johanna Morgan tras recibir "información sobre posibles preocupaciones operativas" en South Chicago Chapel el 31 de julio.</p><p>El IDFPR abrió una queja, inspeccionó el lugar y suspendió su licencia el 5 de agosto por presuntamente permitir que "los difuntos se conservaran en un área sin refrigeración en condiciones deplorables, incluida una infestación de roedores, causando descomposición e infestación de larvas en los cuerpos".</p><p>Clark Morgan acompañó a los investigadores por la casa, según un informe de la Policía de Chicago. Un abogado de la pareja no ha hecho comentarios.</p><p>Además de los 56 cuerpos hallados en South Chicago Chapel, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/08/10/cremated-remains-ashes-found-south-chicago-chapel-funeral-home-95th-street-south-deering-decomposing-bodies" target="_blank" >las autoridades también encontraron 56 cajas con restos cremados</a>, confirmaron los funcionarios el lunes.</p><p>Un portavoz de la Oficina del Médico Forense del Condado de Cook dijo que están custodiando los restos cremados hallados en la funeraria, y que el Departamento de Policía de Chicago (CPD) está localizando a los parientes más cercanos de esos restos.</p><p>La oficina del forense había identificado positivamente 11 de los 56 cuerpos hallados en la funeraria, y 10 de esas familias han sido notificadas. Dos cuerpos ya habían sido entregados a nuevas funerarias. Las autoridades seguían trabajando para identificar los 45 restantes.</p><p>"Si bien el IDFPR emite licencias y regula a los directores funerarios, y no regula las funerarias ni los crematorios, el Departamento se comunica de forma regular y pronta con la Oficina de la Contralora de Illinois, con las fuerzas del orden estatales y locales y con otros socios locales para abordar cualquier forma de conducta conocida indebida", dijo Treto.</p><p>En un evento de campaña no relacionado en el sur del estado el lunes, el gobernador Pritzker dijo: "la oficina de la contralora hizo lo que debía hacer con el crematorio. El IDFPR hizo lo que se supone que debe hacer con respecto a una funeraria y a los directores funerarios, y por tanto eso, creo, aparentemente se manejó correctamente... Estamos hablando de algunos actores realmente malos".</p><h3>Molestia en el vecindario</h3><p>Los vecinos se quejaron durante mucho tiempo de un hedor y de moscas que provenían de la funeraria. Pero el concejal local Peter Chico (10.°) dijo que el olor pudo haber sido enmascarado por otra molestia cercana que ha producido olores intensos en los últimos meses: Pullman Innovations, empresa manufacturera que procesa aceites comestibles para convertirlos en ingredientes para alimento animal.</p><p>Ese olor fue el tema de una reunión comunitaria el 20 de mayo en el distrito del sureste de "Ha sido un problema continuo por 50 años con la empresa antes de eso... y después de que Pullman se hiciera cargo".</p><p>Chico destacó que las únicas quejas que su oficina recibió sobre South Chicago Chapel —antes del espantoso hallazgo de la semana pasada— se enfocaban en "velorios de pandillas que se hacían" en la instalación, ahora cerrada.</p><p>"Cuando comenzaron a operar, había grandes multitudes de personas afuera y los miembros de la comunidad se quejaron. Empezó probablemente hace siete u ocho meses", señaló Chico.</p><p>"Alertamos al Departamento de Policía de Chicago. Han estado allí monitoreando los velorios… Enviaron oficiales para dialogar con los propietarios. Incluso pedimos a la funeraria que proporcionara seguridad", pero nunca se hizo.</p><p>Aunque está horrorizado por el hallazgo de la semana pasada y por la agonía que ha agravado para las familias en duelo, Chico dijo que cree que hizo todo lo posible a nivel local.</p><p>"Les pedimos que fueran más respetuosos con la comunidad en la que operan. Dijeron que iban a trabajar en ello. Dijeron que serían considerados. Dijeron que iban a ser un buen socio", contó Chico. "Llevarlos a la comunidad. Involucrar a la policía. De mi parte, hice todo lo que pude".</p><p>Hasta la noche del lunes, otra funeraria seguía anunciando su negocio en 2939 E. 95th St. Una persona que contestó el teléfono dijo que la funeraria tenía una relación limitada de contratista con South Chicago Chapel, pero no quiso describir más sus vínculos. El director funerario de esa funeraria fue reprendido y multado por el IDFPR en 2019 "por no presentar un certificado de defunción en tiempo y forma".</p><p>Los impuestos sobre la propiedad no se han pagado en la capilla en los últimos dos años, muestran los registros del condado. El gerente de una empresa que antes recibía la factura del impuesto a la propiedad dijo que vendieron el edificio en 2023.</p><p><i>Contribuyeron: Elijah James, Mariah Woelfel e Isabela Nieto </i></p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Rare half-male, half-female bird spotted at suburban Chicago preserve
entries.summary: <p>Local researchers and bird-lovers were in awe this spring when they spotted a rare bird with both male and female characteristics at a nature preserve in suburban Barrington.</p><p>The mysterious bird was a bobolink, and was identified as a bilateral gynandromorph: The bird’s body was divided down the middle, with one side having male characteristics, and the other side female.</p><p>Luke Dahlberg, a conservation seed program manager with Citizens for Conservation and a longtime birder, first encountered the bird May 10 at the organization’s Hill ’N Dale Preserve. Due to its dual color, he named it “Black and Tan,” and experts say its discovery can help provide a greater look into the condition.</p><p>Dahlberg was photographing bobolinks as they returned to the area for the summer when he noticed one bird that looked different from the others. </p><p>At first, he thought the unusual coloring might have been caused by molting.</p><p>When he returned to the same spot weeks later, he saw the bird once again and could immediately tell the bird was divided. In nature, male bobolinks have distinctive black-and-white breeding plumage, while females have more muted brown and golden coloring. Black and Tan displayed both patterns, making the bird immediately recognizable.</p><p>“It was just straight down the middle,” Dahlberg said.</p><p>Dahlberg consulted other bird experts, including members of the Illinois Ornithological Society, who confirmed his suspicions.</p><p>Brian Peer, a biology professor and ornithologist at Stephen F. Austin State University, told <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/in-the-loop-with-sasha-ann-simons/2026/08/11/just-how-rare-is-this-half-female-half-male-bird-sighting" target="_blank" >WBEZ</a> Tuesday morning that gynandromorphism is believed to result from an error during meiosis, which is the process that produces egg cells.</p><p>Within this mutation, the resulting bird has male and female genetic characteristics that’s shown on separate parts of its body.</p><p>Peer told WBEZ the phenomenon is extremely rare, with only about 30 to 40 observations of gynandromorphic wild birds, but the number could be higher as it is difficult to detect and is most noticeable in species where males and females have distinctly different appearances.</p><p>Peer previously co-authored a study documenting a bilateral gynandromorphic northern cardinal observed in northwestern Illinois from 2008 through 2010. The bird was monitored over three separate winters, providing researchers with detailed information about its behavior.</p><p>According to Dahlberg, Black and Tan had established a territory at Hill ’N Dale, allowing other volunteers to observe the bird throughout the summer.</p><p>Black and Tan behaved largely like a male bobolink, singing a song often associated with male members of the species.</p><p>Observers also saw the bird interacting with a female and carrying insects to a location where nesting activity appeared to be taking place.</p><p>These observations could potentially help researchers better understand how gynandromorphic birds behave and whether their behavior more closely resembles that of males, females or a combination of both.</p><p>“Every time that we see one of these birds, it really contributes to our knowledge of that kind of phenomenon because it is so exceedingly rare,” Peer said.</p><p>The bird is no longer at the preserve, but Dahlberg hopes it returns next spring.</p><p>Bobolinks migrate thousands of miles between their breeding grounds in the northern United States and southern Canada and their wintering grounds in southern Brazil and northern Argentina.</p>

entries.title: Lakers sold for record $12.5 billion to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger
entries.summary: <p>LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Lakers are being sold for the second time in a year, going to businessmen Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for a record-breaking price.</p><p>This sale agreement is $12.5 billion, according to a person familiar with the terms who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity Wednesday because neither side revealed specific details of the latest stunning development with one of North America's marquee sports teams.</p><p>ESPN first reported that Kushner and Iger are buying the NBA's most valuable franchise. The Lakers were valued last year at $10 billion — a record for a pro sports team — when Mark Walter purchased a controlling stake from the Buss family, which had owned the team since 1979.</p><p>"As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honored for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world," Iger and Kushner said in a statement. "We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss. Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles."</p><p>Kushner, a venture capitalist, and former Walt Disney Company CEO Iger had been working together on landing a possible NBA expansion team for Las Vegas. By buying the Lakers, they don't have to wait until the possibility of expansion in the 2028-29 season at the earliest.</p><p>Lakers icon Magic Johnson, a partner in Walter's ownership of baseball's Los Angeles Dodgers, praised the deal on social media.</p><p>"Laker fans, you couldn't have two better owners," Johnson wrote. "I've known Bob personally for over 40 years — he has always loved the Lakers and basketball and he will bring championships back to LA."</p><p>The sale still will need approval from the NBA's board of governors, and that process can take several weeks. The next board meeting is set for September in New York.</p><p>The $12.5 billion price tag is not only a record for U.S. pro sports but a new summit in skyrocketing NBA franchise values. Only three years ago, Michael Jordan sold his majority stake in the Charlotte Hornets for a $3 billion valuation, while the Boston Celtics were sold last year to private equity mogul Bill Chisholm at a valuation of just over $6 billion.</p><p>Walter's agreement to purchase a controlling stake in the Lakers at the $10 billion valuation last summer obliterated that mark, and now Iger and Kushner have pushed the bar even higher.</p><p>The 66-year-old Walter's shocking decision to sell after just 10 months of official ownership is reverberating throughout the team's massive fan base, which appeared to be uniformly excited about the purchase last year. Walter has stewarded the Dodgers into the most successful stretch in franchise history, with three World Series championships in the past six seasons as the most aggressive spenders in baseball.</p><p>Multiple media outlets last month reported that Walter's business empire is under scrutiny from both federal prosecutors and the Securities and Exchange Commission in tax fraud investigations.</p><p>The Lakers are 17-time NBA champions who won their most recent title in 2020. They've made the playoffs in each of the past four seasons, and their current roster is built around NBA scoring champion Luka Doncic, who is signed through the 2028-29 season. The Slovenian superstar has become passionate about Los Angeles and the Lakers less than two years after his arrival.</p><p>"Being a Laker means everything to me, and I'm excited to get back on the court and bring a championship to LA," Doncic wrote on social media after hearing of the sale. "I've gotten used to big changes over these last few years, but I know that no matter what, there is no limit to the potential of this iconic franchise. I look forward to meeting Josh and Bob so we can get to work building something special in LA together."</p><p>The 41-year-old Kushner has been a minority owner of two NBA teams, but he jumped into the international sports spotlight this summer when his capital holding company, Thrive Eternal, was set to be the "anchor investor" in FIFA President Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in future World Cup profits. Infantino abandoned the idea on July 31.</p><p>Kushner's older brother is Jared Kushner, son-in-law of U.S. President Donald Trump.</p><p>Josh Kushner currently owns a minority stake in the Miami Heat, and he previously owned a stake in the Memphis Grizzlies.</p><p>The 75-year-old Iger became one of Hollywood's most well-known executives while he ran Disney for two lengthy stints between 2005 and last March, when he stepped aside. Iger and his wife, former sports journalist Willow Bay, became the controlling owners of NWSL team Angel City FC in 2024 with a deal that valued the club at $250 million.</p><p>Walter's purchase of the Lakers was approved by NBA owners last October. He originally bought a 27% minority stake in the team in 2021 before purchasing control of the team last year.</p><p>The Lakers' 17 championships going back to the franchise's origin in Minneapolis are the second-most in NBA history behind Boston's 18. It is a global brand, always at or near the top of the league's merchandise-sales rankings.</p><p>This record sale price comes just weeks after LeBron James, the league's all-time leading scorer, left the Lakers after eight seasons to become a free agent. James ultimately decided to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers.</p><p>Walter and his team had already begun to make extensive changes to the Lakers, who were often perceived as an antiquated franchise in many aspects during their decades of Buss family ownership.</p><p>The Lakers had beefed up their basketball operations department with new hires in the front office around longtime general manager Rob Pelinka. They also boosted the business side with extensive searches for new revenue, including sales of new jersey patches and additional prominent sponsorship deals.</p><p>When Walter bought his controlling interest in the Lakers, the deal specified that Jeanie Buss would stay on as the team's governor. With new ownership, it's unclear whether Buss will have a continuing role in the team she inherited along with her siblings from her father, Jerry Buss, who died in 2013.</p><p>Along with the Dodgers, Walter and his various partners also have ownership interests in the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks, English Premier League club Chelsea, the Professional Women's Hockey League and the new Cadillac Formula 1 racing team.<br></p>
